1a.title: Calculate Vertical Support Reaction R_A for Simply Supported UDL Beam
1a.promptTitle: Calculate Vertical Support Reaction R_A for Simply Supported UDL Beam
1a.promptLead: A simply supported steel floor beam spans L = 6.0 m between pinned support A and roller support B. It carries a uniform distributed load w = 4.0 kN/m across its full length. Calculate the vertical support reaction R_A at support A.
1a.promptBody: A simply supported steel floor beam spans L = 6.0 m between pinned support A and roller support B. It carries a uniform distributed load w = 4.0 kN/m across its full length. Calculate the vertical support reaction R_A at support A.

promptFormula.rhsNote: by symmetry for a full-span UDL

1a.diagramCaption: Simply supported beam spanning L = 6.0 m under uniform load w = 4.0 kN/m.
hints: First compute the total resultant vertical force W = w × L acting over the 6.0 m span.
By symmetry, the resultant W acts at midspan (x = L / 2), so R_A = R_B = W / 2 in kN.

parallelExample.title: Parallel Example: 8.0 m Span with w = 5.0 kN/m UDL
parallelExample.givenText: A simply supported beam spans L = 8.0 m and carries a uniform load w = 5.0 kN/m over its full length.

steps.heading: Share equally between symmetric supports A and B

fullSolutionSteps.heading: Compute total resultant downward load W on the 6.0 m span

1b.title: Calculate Maximum Midspan Sagging Moment M_max
1b.promptTitle: Calculate Maximum Midspan Sagging Moment M_max
1b.promptLead: For the 6.0 m simply supported beam carrying a uniform distributed load w = 4.0 kN/m (with vertical reactions R_A = R_B = 12.0 kN), calculate the peak sagging bending moment M_max at midspan (x = 3.0 m).
1b.promptBody: For the 6.0 m simply supported beam carrying a uniform distributed load w = 4.0 kN/m (with vertical reactions R_A = R_B = 12.0 kN), calculate the peak sagging bending moment M_max at midspan (x = 3.0 m).

promptFormula.rhsNote: at midspan x = L / 2 where V(x) = 0

1b.diagramCaption: Parabolic Bending Moment Diagram plotted on the bottom tension face peaking at x = 3.0 m.
hints: Take a free-body cut at midspan x = L / 2 where shear force V(x) = 0.
Evaluate M_max = R_A × (L / 2) − (w × L / 2) × (L / 4), or substitute w and L into w·L² / 8.

parallelExample.title: Parallel Example: 8.0 m Span with w = 5.0 kN/m UDL
parallelExample.givenText: A simply supported beam of span L = 8.0 m carries a uniform distributed load w = 5.0 kN/m.

fullSolutionSteps.heading: Take moments to the left of midspan cut x = 3.0 m

2a.title: Calculate Extreme Fibre Bending Stress σ_max (in MPa)
2a.promptTitle: Calculate Extreme Fibre Bending Stress σ_max (in MPa)
2a.promptLead: The beam carries a peak sagging bending moment M_max = 18.0 kN·m. Its cross-section is a solid 100 mm × 200 mm rectangle with second moment of area I_xx = 6.67 × 10⁷ mm⁴ and elastic section modulus W_el = b·d²/6 = 6.67 × 10⁵ mm³ (667 cm³). Calculate the maximum longitudinal bending stress σ_max at the extreme fibre (y_max = 100 mm).
2a.promptBody: The beam carries a peak sagging bending moment M_max = 18.0 kN·m. Its cross-section is a solid 100 mm × 200 mm rectangle with second moment of area I_xx = 6.67 × 10⁷ mm⁴ and elastic section modulus W_el = b·d²/6 = 6.67 × 10⁵ mm³ (667 cm³). Calculate the maximum longitudinal bending stress σ_max at the extreme fibre (y_max = 100 mm).

promptFormula.rhsNote: Convert M_max to N·mm (× 10⁶) so N·mm / mm³ gives N/mm² = MPa

givenData: Width b = 100 mm, Depth d = 200 mm
Elastic modulus W_el = b·d²/6 = 6.67 × 10⁵ mm³ (667 cm³)
2a.diagramCaption: Rectangular section 100 mm × 200 mm (W_el = 6.67 × 10⁵ mm³) with linear elastic bending stress distribution.
hints: Convert the peak bending moment M_max from kN·m into N·mm first by multiplying by 10⁶ (since 1 kN = 10³ N and 1 m = 10³ mm).
Apply Navier's flexure formula σ_max = M_max / W_el by dividing the converted moment in N·mm by the elastic section modulus W_el = b·d²/6 in mm³ so the units reduce to N/mm² (MPa).

parallelExample.title: Parallel Example: M = 12.0 kN·m on a 100 mm × 200 mm Section
parallelExample.givenText: A 100 mm × 200 mm section (W_el = 6.67 × 10⁵ mm³) resists a bending moment of M = 12.0 kN·m.

steps.heading: Convert bending moment from kN·m to N·mm
Divide by elastic section modulus W_el = b·d²/6

fullSolutionSteps.heading: Convert M_max = 18.0 kN·m to consistent N·mm
Evaluate elastic section modulus W_el = b·d² / 6
Compute extreme fibre stress σ_max = M_max / W_el

2a-R.title: Warm-Up Drill: Convert kN·m to N·mm Before Dividing by W_el
2a-R.promptTitle: Warm-Up Drill: Convert kN·m to N·mm Before Dividing by W_el
2a-R.promptLead: To eliminate the 10³ / 10⁶ unit conversion slip, calculate the extreme fibre stress σ in MPa when the same 100 mm × 200 mm section (W_el = 6.67 × 10⁵ mm³) carries a bending moment of M = 6.0 kN·m (= 6.0 × 10⁶ N·mm).
2a-R.promptBody: To eliminate the 10³ / 10⁶ unit conversion slip, calculate the extreme fibre stress σ in MPa when the same 100 mm × 200 mm section (W_el = 6.67 × 10⁵ mm³) carries a bending moment of M = 6.0 kN·m (= 6.0 × 10⁶ N·mm).
2a-R.diagramCaption: Unit consistency drill: 6.0 × 10⁶ N·mm divided by W_el = 6.67 × 10⁵ mm³.
hints: Express both the bending moment M (in N·mm) and the elastic section modulus W_el = b·d²/6 (in mm³) in scientific notation before dividing.
Cancel the common powers of ten between the numerator (N·mm) and denominator (mm³) to evaluate σ = M / W_el in N/mm² (MPa).

parallelExample.title: Parallel Example: M = 4.0 kN·m on W_el = 6.67 × 10⁵ mm³

steps.heading: Divide in consistent N and mm units

fullSolutionSteps.heading: Divide M in N·mm by W_el in mm³

2b.title: Verify Midspan Vertical Deflection δ_max (in mm)
2b.promptTitle: Verify Midspan Vertical Deflection δ_max (in mm)
2b.promptLead: For the 6.0 m (= 6,000 mm) simply supported beam under unfactored SLS uniform load w = 4.0 kN/m (= 4.0 N/mm), with Young’s modulus E = 210,000 MPa (N/mm²) and second moment of area I = 8.10 × 10⁷ mm⁴, calculate the midspan vertical deflection δ_max.
2b.promptBody: For the 6.0 m (= 6,000 mm) simply supported beam under unfactored SLS uniform load w = 4.0 kN/m (= 4.0 N/mm), with Young’s modulus E = 210,000 MPa (N/mm²) and second moment of area I = 8.10 × 10⁷ mm⁴, calculate the midspan vertical deflection δ_max.

promptFormula.rhsNote: Use w in N/mm and L in mm so δ_max is in mm

2b.diagramCaption: Elastic deflected shape under serviceability UDL w = 4.0 N/mm.
hints: Express all quantities in N and mm: w = 4.0 N/mm, L = 6,000 mm, E = 210,000 N/mm², and I = 8.10 × 10⁷ mm⁴.
Substitute these consistent N and mm values into δ_max = (5 · w · L⁴) / (384 · E · I) so the units cancel directly to mm.

parallelExample.title: Parallel Example: 5.0 m Span with w = 3.0 N/mm
parallelExample.givenText: A beam spanning L = 5,000 mm with E = 210,000 MPa and I = 8.10 × 10⁷ mm⁴ carries w = 3.0 N/mm.

steps.heading: Substitute N and mm values into 5wL⁴ / (384EI)

fullSolutionSteps.heading: Evaluate numerator 5 · w · L⁴ in N·mm³

2c.title: Combined Midspan Bending Moment (UDL + Central Point Load)
2c.promptTitle: Combined Midspan Bending Moment (UDL + Central Point Load)
2c.promptLead: In addition to the uniform load w = 4.0 kN/m over the 6.0 m span (which gives M_udl = 18.0 kN·m at midspan), a secondary trimmer beam applies a central point load P = 10.0 kN at x = 3.0 m. Calculate the total peak midspan bending moment M_total.
2c.promptBody: In addition to the uniform load w = 4.0 kN/m over the 6.0 m span (which gives M_udl = 18.0 kN·m at midspan), a secondary trimmer beam applies a central point load P = 10.0 kN at x = 3.0 m. Calculate the total peak midspan bending moment M_total.

promptFormula.rhsNote: Plus central point load contribution (P · L) / 4

2c.diagramCaption: Combined UDL (4.0 kN/m) and central point load (P = 10.0 kN) on a 6.0 m simple span.
hints: Compute the midspan bending moment from the central point load alone using M_point = (P × L) / 4.
By linear superposition at x = L / 2, sum the UDL midspan moment M_udl and the central point-load moment M_point in kN·m.

parallelExample.title: Parallel Example: M_udl = 20.0 kN·m + Central P = 8.0 kN on L = 6.0 m
parallelExample.givenText: Combine M_udl = 20.0 kN·m with P = 8.0 kN at midspan on a 6.0 m span.

fullSolutionSteps.heading: Calculate point load moment M_point = P·L / 4
Add co-existing UDL midspan moment M_udl = 18.0 kN·m

3.title: Calculate Peak Neutral-Axis Shear Stress τ_max
3.promptTitle: Calculate Peak Neutral-Axis Shear Stress τ_max
3.promptLead: At the support of the 100 mm × 200 mm rectangular section (area A = 20,000 mm²), the combined vertical shear force is V_max = 17.0 kN (= 17,000 N). Calculate the peak parabolic shear stress τ_max at the neutral axis.
3.promptBody: At the support of the 100 mm × 200 mm rectangular section (area A = 20,000 mm²), the combined vertical shear force is V_max = 17.0 kN (= 17,000 N). Calculate the peak parabolic shear stress τ_max at the neutral axis.

promptFormula.rhsNote: Peak neutral-axis shear stress in a rectangle is 1.5 × (V / A)

3.diagramCaption: Rectangular section 100 mm × 200 mm under vertical shear V_max = 17.0 kN.
hints: Convert V_max from kN into Newtons and divide by the cross-sectional area A = b·d in mm² to obtain the average shear stress in N/mm² (MPa).
Multiply the average shear stress V / A by the rectangular parabolic factor 3/2 (1.5) to find the peak shear stress at the neutral axis.

parallelExample.title: Parallel Example: V = 12.0 kN on a 100 mm × 200 mm Section
parallelExample.givenText: Compute peak shear stress τ_max = 1.5 × V / (b·d) for V = 12,000 N.

4.title: Calculate Factored ULS Design Load Intensity w_Ed
4.promptTitle: Calculate Factored ULS Design Load Intensity w_Ed
4.promptLead: If the beam’s unfactored loading consists of characteristic permanent dead load G_k = 2.5 kN/m and characteristic variable floor load Q_k = 1.5 kN/m, calculate the factored Ultimate Limit State (ULS) design load w_Ed using γ_G = 1.35 and γ_Q = 1.50.
4.promptBody: If the beam’s unfactored loading consists of characteristic permanent dead load G_k = 2.5 kN/m and characteristic variable floor load Q_k = 1.5 kN/m, calculate the factored Ultimate Limit State (ULS) design load w_Ed using γ_G = 1.35 and γ_Q = 1.50.
4.diagramCaption: Factored ULS design line load w_Ed = 1.35 G_k + 1.50 Q_k.
hints: Multiply the characteristic permanent action G_k by γ_G = 1.35 and the characteristic variable action Q_k by γ_Q = 1.50.
Sum the factored permanent and variable line-load components to obtain the combined ULS design load w_Ed in kN/m.

parallelExample.title: Parallel Example: G_k = 3.0 kN/m and Q_k = 2.0 kN/m
parallelExample.givenText: Combine G_k = 3.0 kN/m and Q_k = 2.0 kN/m at ULS.

5a.title: Compute Parabolic BMD Area ∫ M(x) dx by Simpson’s 1/3 Rule
5a.promptTitle: Compute Parabolic BMD Area ∫ M(x) dx by Simpson’s 1/3 Rule
5a.promptLead: To verify moment-area curvature independently, compute the total area ∫ M(x) dx under the symmetric parabolic bending moment diagram over the span L = 6.0 m when M(0) = 0, M(3.0) = 18.0 kN·m, and M(6.0) = 0.
5a.promptBody: To verify moment-area curvature independently, compute the total area ∫ M(x) dx under the symmetric parabolic bending moment diagram over the span L = 6.0 m when M(0) = 0, M(3.0) = 18.0 kN·m, and M(6.0) = 0.
5a.diagramCaption: Parabolic BMD area integration over L = 6.0 m.
hints: For a symmetric quadratic parabola of base L and peak height M_max, the enclosed area equals two-thirds of the bounding rectangle.
Substitute M_max (in kN·m) and L (in m) into Area_M = (2 / 3) × M_max × L to obtain the moment area in kN·m².
